name: Abu Atika Tarif ibn Salman
nameAr: أبو عاتكة طَريف بن سَلْمان، ويقال ابن سليمان، ويقال سلمان بن طريف

nisbas.en: al-Basri (so Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bukhari; the Taqrib: "Basran or Kufan")

diedNote: second century; death year not securely recorded

taqrib.en: Weak; al-Sulaymani went further against him.

teachers.name: Anas ibn Malik
teachers.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib (Hyderabad ed.) 2/294, OpenITI transcription of Shamela 3310, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenITI/0875AH/master/data/0852IbnHajarCasqalani/0852IbnHajarCasqalani.TahdhibTahdhib/0852IbnHajarCasqalani.TahdhibTahdhib.Shamela0003310-ara2 (al-Hasan ibn Atiyya's entry; Jami' al-Tirmidhi 726)

students.name: al-Hasan ibn Atiyya ibn Najih
students.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib (Hyderabad ed.) 2/294, OpenITI transcription of Shamela 3310, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenITI/0875AH/master/data/0852IbnHajarCasqalani/0852IbnHajarCasqalani.TahdhibTahdhib/0852IbnHajarCasqalani.TahdhibTahdhib.Shamela0003310-ara2 (al-Hasan ibn Atiyya's entry; Jami' al-Tirmidhi 726)

verdicts.en: Objectionable in hadith. (One of al-Bukhari's severest formulae: he said that anyone he describes this way may not be narrated from.)
His hadith is gone; weak in hadith.

verdicts.ar: منكر الحديث جدًا، يروي عن أنس ما لا يشبه حديثه
verdicts.en: Very objectionable in hadith; he transmits from Anas things that do not resemble Anas's hadith.

verdicts.ar: وعامة ما يرويه عن أنس لا يتابعه عليه أحد من الثقات
verdicts.en: Most of what he transmits from Anas, no reliable narrator corroborates him in.

verdicts.source: listed in his al-Du'afa wa al-Matrukin; the word as reported in Tahdhib al-Kamal

verdicts.ar: لا يعرف أبو العاتكة ولا يدرى من أين هو، فليس لهذا الحديث أصل
verdicts.en: Abu Atika is not known, nor where he is from; so this hadith has no basis.

verdicts.ar: مختلف في اسمه، مجمع على ضعفه
verdicts.en: His name is disputed; his weakness is agreed upon.
verdicts.source: al-Mughni fi al-Du'afa 2/793; al-Kashif: “they weakened him”

flags.label: The link on which the report fails
flags.detail: Every verdict on “even in China” is a verdict on this man. Al-Tirmidhi transmitted a single hadith from him; no major critic defended him.

bio: A narrator from Anas ibn Malik whose name the sources could not even fix (Tarif ibn Salman, Tarif ibn Sulayman, or Salman ibn Tarif). Al-Dhahabi noted that he is “the author of the hadith ‘seek knowledge even in China’, and better known by his kunya”.
